lyrics:
[Intro: soft steady drums, round bass, two drifting guitar chords]

[Verse 1: husky, calm, close]
So you want the open road
The wind and none of the weight
Go on, then, I won't hold the door
I won't stand at the gate

[Pre-Chorus: vibraphone, soft harmony]
One night the engine's going to cool
And the radio will fade
And you'll be parked with what you chose
And everything it weighed

[Chorus: three-part harmony, the same two chords]
Tides only turn when nobody's looking
Fires only talk when the room goes cold
You'll hear it when it's quiet
What the loud was keeping from you
And I'll be fine by then
Oh, I'll be fine

[Verse 2: husky, a little cooler]
I've seen the way you pack a bag
Like the bag has all the answers
You love the leaving more than the going
You're a dance without the dancers

[Pre-Chorus: vibraphone, soft harmony]
One day the mirror's going to ask
And you won't know what to say
And you'll remember someone asked you
Kindly, once, to stay

[Chorus: three-part harmony, the same two chords]
Tides only turn when nobody's looking
Fires only talk when the room goes cold
You'll hear it when it's quiet
What the loud was keeping from you
And I'll be fine by then
Oh, I'll be fine

[Guitar Solo: volume swells, sparse and sighing]

[Final Chorus: harmonies fuller, ad-libs drifting]
Tides only turn when nobody's looking
Fires only talk when the room goes cold
You'll hear it when it's quiet
You'll hear it when it's quiet

[Outro: drums and bass alone, fading]
Quiet
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 120 BPM, 4/4, A minor. Two chords alternating without change for the whole song. Cool, floating and unhurried.

VOICE: Female alto, husky and slightly nasal with a quick, fluttering vibrato. She sings softly and evenly, never pushing. Two more voices, a higher woman and a man, join in close three-part harmony on the choruses. Dreamy ad-libs over the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A very steady, soft drum pattern with a constant hi-hat and a gentle snare. A round, simple, repeating bass line. Clean electric guitar playing swells and small answering phrases with a volume pedal. Vibraphone. Electric piano. Acoustic guitar strummed quietly. Light congas.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, drums, bass and guitar. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:48 Pre-chorus. 1:20 Chorus 1. 1:52 Verse 2. 2:24 Pre-chorus. 2:56 Chorus 2. 3:28 Guitar solo of swells. 3:44 Final chorus, with the title line repeated. 4:08 Outro, drums and bass fading by 4:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1970s California studio sound: dry, close, warm and perfectly balanced, each instrument small and clear, a lot of air.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first chorus, when three voices arrive on the proverb lines.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: She does not predict that he will be lonely and come back. She says she will be fine by then. The calm of the original is kept, and the dependence is taken out.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Composure, clear sight, release.
